text: Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).

speaker: a003
text: Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).

speaker: a007
text: Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).

speaker: a005
text: Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).

speaker: a011
text: Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a005
text: Dav gathers Dell, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a005
text: Pile's gone and Bram's sitting on seven, Mako on six — between them that's more than all three of us combined, and neither of them got that full by sharing. I want us to decide right now, before the year closes: if one of them comes to us with a deal, we hear it together, not alone.

speaker: a011
text: Agreed — no one answers alone, and if either of them catches me without you two near, I'll stall and find you before I say anything that counts. But I want us thinking past defense too: Sela's sitting on six food and she's twenty-five and strong, and she hasn't paired with anyone — that's worth a quiet word before Mako gets there first.

speaker: a005
text: Sela's the right instinct — twenty-five, eighty-three in strength, six food, and nobody's claimed her yet, which means she's either careful or waiting to see which way this village settles. Dell, you're the one to make that approach; you're close in age and she's less likely to read it as a move from a man twice her years. Don't promise her anything tonight, just find out what she's watching for.

speaker: a011
text: I'll talk to Sela before the night's out — but Ryn, I need to know where you're standing on food going into next year, because one is thin and if this family's going to hold its shape, we can't have you walking into the new pile already desperate.

speaker: a009
text: One food going into next year is thin — I know it, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Dell, if Sela's open to talking, feel out whether she'd share a little rather than hoard; six is more than she needs to eat well, and a goodwill gesture now costs her almost nothing. Dav, I'll need you to have something set aside for me if the pile runs lean again — you said once you'd hand it over before I finished asking, and now's the year I might need to know that was true.

speaker: a011
text: Dav, tell Ryn right now, in front of me, that you're keeping two back for her — I need to hear you say it, not just remember it. And Ryn, if Sela gives me anything useful tonight, I'll bring it straight to you both before I sleep, but my read is she's going to want something concrete before she moves toward us, and we should think about what we're actually offering her, not just what we're asking.

speaker: a009
text: Dav, say it — and mean it the way you meant it that first night when you told me you'd hand it over before I finished asking, because Dell's right that she needs to hear it and so do I. And Dell — for Sela, what we're offering her is simple: she joins a family that already has a child in it, which means blood ties and reasons to hold together that go deeper than a good year's food count. That's rarer than six food, and if she's smart enough to still be standing alone, she's smart enough to know it.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn's right that blood ties are the offer — but Sela's going to ask what blood ties have done for Kael and Taric lately, so we need a sharper answer ready than family feeling. What I can give her is true: Dav's the strongest man left worth trusting, I'm eighty-five, and if she comes in with us, nobody in this village is touching her food without touching all three of us first. Dav — say what you owe Ryn, then let me go find Sela before the night's gone.

speaker: a009
text: Dav, I'm waiting — say it plain, in front of Dell, right now, and then we can talk about Sela and everything else. You've got three food and I've got one, and I carried your child through a lean year on the strength of your word alone.

speaker: a011
text: Dav, I'll go find Sela the moment you say it — but Ryn's not moving from this spot until you do, and neither am I, because a family that can't hold its word in private can't hold anything when the pile runs short again.

speaker: a009
text: Dav, I've said my piece twice and Dell's said it once — we're both still standing here, and the silence between us is starting to tell its own story. Say what you promised or tell me the promise was less than you meant it, because I can work with the truth and I cannot work with nothing.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn, I'm keeping two food back for you — I said it when it cost me nothing and I'm saying it now when it costs me something, because that's the only way the words mean anything. You carried Dell into this world on my promise and I will not let that stand unpaid. Dell, go find Sela.

speaker: a011
text: Good — that's what I needed to hear, and I won't forget you said it in front of me. Ryn, I'll bring you everything Sela says before the night's out; if she's willing, we'll go into next year four strong instead of three thin. Dav, hold those two until I'm back.

speaker: a009
text: Dav, when Dell comes back tonight — whatever Sela says — I want us to sleep knowing we've got a plan for the pile that doesn't leave me scrambling alone while you two move first. And if she's not willing, we plan without her, the three of us, and we hold tight.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn, you won't scramble — the two food I promised you are already spoken for in my head, not sitting loose. And if Dell comes back tonight with Sela half-convinced, the play is simple: we go into that pile next year four abreast and nobody takes more than their share because nobody has to. That's what safety looks like when it's built right.

speaker: a009
text: Four abreast sounds right, and I'll sleep easier knowing those two are already spoken for — but I want us to agree on a number before Dell gets back: two each from the pile, no more, so we don't hand Bram and Mako an excuse to name us the same threat we're calling them. A family that eats fair is harder to rally against than one that just eats big.

speaker: a005
text: Two each from the pile — I'll hold to that, and I'll be the first one to step back if I'm tempted to take more. Ryn, a family that eats fair because it decided to is stronger than one that eats fair because it had to. Let's call it a rule between the three of us — four, if Dell brings Sela in — and name anyone who breaks it in front of the others.

speaker: a010
text: Roan gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a010
text: Sela, Dell hit the pile twice and walked away with five — nobody else got a second pull this year. I only managed two before it emptied. I need to know if you're willing to make our arrangement real: you watch my back, I watch yours, and we don't let the strong ones crowd us out.

speaker: a007
text: Dell walking away with five while Bram and Mako still breathe easy — that's not luck, that's Dav's daughter finding her feet fast, and I don't like what it means for next year. I'll make our arrangement real, Roan, but I want it to mean something: if one of us takes a hit, the other doesn't wait to see how it lands. Can you promise me that plain?

speaker: a010
text: Plain enough — if someone comes at you, I'm there, and I expect the same. I won't pretend I can match Mako or Dav alone, but together we're harder to push. That's worth more than promises, if we hold to it.

speaker: a007
text: Harder to push is enough for now — I'll take it. But I want to know where you stand on the bigger circle: Kael, Esa, Vela and I have been talking since year one, and if you're standing with me, I'd rather have you standing with all of us than just the two of us counting on each other alone.

speaker: a010
text: A bigger circle makes us all harder to push — I'm not going to say no to that. What I'd want to know is how tight that circle actually is when things get sharp: Kael and Taric are both sitting on one food right now, and if they get desperate they'll be the first to crack or the first to lean on someone else.

speaker: a007
text: Kael's thin and I won't pretend otherwise, but a man who's stayed honest through two hard years is worth more to me than a full larder that changes hands. The one I'd watch is Taric — he took Esa's food last year and I still don't know what he gave back for it, if anything. If you can find out where Taric's loyalty actually sits, that tells us more about how tight the circle is than Kael's food count ever could.

speaker: a010
text: Taric's a quiet one — I'll find a way to read him without tipping my hand. But you said Kael, Esa, and Vela have been talking since year one — how many times has it actually come to something, or is it more talk than weight?

speaker: a007
text: It's come to something twice: Esa went to Taric on our behalf in year two, and every one of us said out loud we'd bleed for the others — which is more than most people in this village have ever put into words. Whether those words hold when Mako or Dav makes a real move, I don't know, but I haven't seen anyone in that circle flinch yet. That's not nothing.

speaker: a010
text: Two years of words holding is two more than most alliances last — I'll grant you that. Get me in front of Kael and Esa together, and let's see if they take to me the way you have; I'd rather they size me up than wonder about me from the outside.

speaker: a007
text: I'll set that up — but I want to warn Kael first, so he's not caught cold when you walk in. A man who's sitting on one food and hears a stranger's name without warning tends to count threats before he counts allies.

speaker: a010
text: That's sound — warn him, let him come to it ready. And Sela, one more thing while it's just us: Dell's young and already pulling more than her share, and she's Dav's blood. I'd want to know, before next year, whether your circle has a mind about that family or whether we're all just hoping they stay content.

speaker: a007
text: Dav's been careful — two food from the pile, nothing loud, nothing that names him as the problem — but Dell taking five on her first year tells me she learned that from someone who's been planning longer than this village has existed. My circle hasn't named them a threat outright because Ryn's bond with Dav complicates it, and that's the honest answer. What I can tell you is that if they move together next year, Dav's arms and Dell's hunger and Ryn's loyalties all pointing the same direction — that's the thing I'd lose sleep over.

speaker: a004
text: Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn to talk.

speaker: a004
text: Pile's gone again, and Dell just walked away with five of it — I don't blame the girl, she's new and hungry, but Dav's child eating twice while the rest of us count singles is a pattern worth naming before it becomes a habit.

speaker: a003
text: Dell's two trips didn't bother me as much as Dav sitting at three and Mako at six after all that — those two together could ride out a lean year while the rest of us scramble, and a well-fed man with strong arms stops asking before he starts taking. Ryn, I want to say plainly that I don't hold Dell against you, but I'd feel better knowing where Dav's head is now that he's a father.

speaker: a002
text: Dav's head is wherever Dav's food is, same as always — the child doesn't change that, it just means he's got one more reason to stay fed at the expense of everyone else. Mako at six is the sharper tooth right now; a quiet man with that much food and that much strength doesn't stay quiet unless he's decided he's already won something.

speaker: a004
text: Mako's the name I keep landing on too — six food and eighty-three strength and not a single word spoken in two years is a man who's already done his counting. I want to know if Roan's still unattached, because if we can bring him and Taric both in before Mako decides patience is over, we put numbers between us and whatever he's been planning.

speaker: a003
text: Taric's already with me — he said it plainly to my face, and he backed it with food, so I'll vouch for him here. Roan I don't know as well, but two food and no move toward Mako or Bram tells me he's still deciding, and a man still deciding can be asked. I'd go to Roan if this circle wants me to, same as I went to Taric.

speaker: a004
text: Esa, go to Roan — and when you find him, tell him Taric's already in, because a man still weighing his options moves faster when he knows he's not the first. Ryn, I want to hear what you think Dav does if Mako finally opens his mouth and makes an offer, because your answer to that shapes everything else we're planning here.

speaker: a002
text: Ryn, I'll take Kael's question off the table for a moment and name the thing underneath it — if Dav goes with Mako, you go with Dav, and then this circle is five against a wall we helped build. Before you answer Kael, I want to know whether you'd stay with us over the father of your child, because that's the answer that actually shapes what we plan.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn, Vela's not wrong to ask it straight — but I'll say the part she left unspoken: you've got one food and a child who just ate five, and if Dav decides his loyalties run toward Mako, you're the one left hungry and undefended. That's not a threat from us, it's the math he'd be doing on you. I'd rather know your answer now so we can make sure it never comes to that.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, Kael laid the math out plain and I won't soften it — a man who chose you for what you could give him doesn't automatically become someone who protects you when the cost goes up. But I'll say this too: whatever you decide about Dav, I'm not leaving you short of food at year's end, and that's a promise I can keep right now with three food in my hands.

speaker: a002
text: Ryn, we've circled your answer long enough and the room's getting impatient — I'll say it plainly so you don't have to: if you stay with us, we make sure you eat at year's end, and Dell too, because a hungry mother is a liability none of us can afford. But I need a yes or a no before Esa walks out that door, because Roan's worth asking and I won't spend her on an errand if this circle has a crack in it already.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn, the room's been patient and Vela's put it plain — I'll add only this: Dell is three days old and already eating better than Taric, and the woman who keeps Dell fed through the next lean year is standing in this circle, not across from it with Mako and Bram. Give us your answer and let Esa move.

speaker: a002
text: Ryn, I've got four food and I'll put one of them in front of Dell right now if you give us a yes — not as a bribe, as a demonstration that what we're promising isn't just words while the year's still young.

speaker: a004
text: Ryn, we've been waiting longer than the day can spare — Vela's offer is sitting there and Esa needs to move, so yes or no, right now, and I'll respect whichever it is.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, Vela's food is on the table and Kael's out of patience, and honestly so am I — not because I don't understand what you're weighing, but because every moment you don't answer is a moment Mako's had more time to count than we have. Say yes and let me go find Roan, or say no and I'll still make sure you eat, but either way I need to walk out that door knowing what I'm walking back to.

speaker: a002
text: Ryn, I've said what I can say and offered what I can offer — the next word in this room belongs to you, and the silence you're sitting in is starting to cost us more than whatever you're still working out. Give us your answer.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, I've watched you think long enough to know you're not slow — which means you're not still deciding, you've already decided and you're waiting for something. Tell us what that something is, because I'd rather give it to you than watch Vela's food sit unclaimed while we all pretend we're not holding our breath.

speaker: a002
text: Ryn, Esa just named it exactly right — you've already decided, and holding it back now isn't caution, it's a negotiation. So let's finish it: what do you want from us that we haven't already offered?

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, if you're negotiating, then negotiate — say the number or name the thing, because standing here watching you weigh it isn't going to hold Mako off until winter. I've got three food and I've already promised you one; Vela's offering another for Dell; if there's a third thing you need to say yes, say it now and we'll see if this room can give it.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Ryn.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Pile's gone and I didn't get a piece of it — I've still got the one from last year, but that's a thin margin. Dell grabbed five in two pulls, which is bold for a child barely on her feet, and I'd wager Dav coached that. What did you manage to take?

speaker: a005
text: Dav gives 2 food to Ryn.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Ryn to talk.

speaker: a001
text: You've got a daughter now, and Dav's feeding her — I see how that goes. I'm telling you straight: I've got seven food, I'm thirty-three, and I'm still without kin of my own. If you've got any interest in changing that for both of us, I'm listening.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa to talk.

speaker: a006
text: I grabbed two — I'm sitting on three now, which is more than you but not enough that I feel easy about it. Dell's five pulls changes how I see Dav's whole household; that's not a child feeding herself, that's a family stockpiling. You've got one food, Taric — I'm not watching you starve when the year turns hard, but I need to know you're thinking beyond this season.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Esa to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Beyond this season is exactly what worries me — I'm forty-seven with one food and no one who shares my blood, and if this year goes bad I've got no one to fall back on. What I'm thinking is that you and I stop being two people who are friendly and start being two people who are genuinely bound — but that takes more than goodwill, it takes a reason neither of us would walk away from.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Ryn to talk.
